stem: What is the primary advantage of a spine-leaf data center topology over a traditional three-tier design?
explanation: Spine-leaf provides predictable, low-latency any-to-any connectivity with consistent hop counts (typically 2 hops) between any two leaves, improving east-west traffic performance.

choices.text: Consistent low-latency path between any two endpoints
Eliminates the need for routing protocols
Reduces the number of physical switches required
Provides built-in encryption for all traffic

stem: Which wireless standard operates exclusively in the 6 GHz band?
explanation: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6E) extended Wi-Fi 6 into the 6 GHz band. 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7) also uses 6 GHz among other bands, but 6 GHz exclusivity as a new band was introduced with 6E.

stem: Which 802.11 feature allows a client to remain connected while moving between access points without re-authenticating?
explanation: 802.11r (Fast BSS Transition) enables fast roaming by allowing a client to pre-authenticate with target APs, reducing transition time.

stem: What is the purpose of IPv6 Router Advertisement (RA) Guard?
explanation: RA Guard is a security feature that blocks rogue Router Advertisements on switch ports, preventing attackers from redirecting traffic or performing MITM attacks via fake RAs.

stem: Which campus architecture layer is responsible for connecting end-user devices to the network?
explanation: The access layer connects end-user devices (PCs, phones, APs) to the network and enforces port-level security policies.

stem: Which DTP mode will form a trunk only if the neighboring port is also set to trunk or desirable?
explanation: Dynamic auto forms a trunk only if the neighbor is in trunk or desirable mode. It does not actively initiate trunking.

stem: What is the purpose of storm control on a switch port?
explanation: Storm control monitors traffic levels and drops broadcast/multicast/unicast traffic exceeding configured thresholds, preventing broadcast storms from consuming bandwidth.

choices.text: Limit broadcast/multicast/unicast traffic to prevent storms

stem: Which port security violation mode shuts down the port when an unauthorized MAC is detected?
explanation: Shutdown mode (default) err-disables the port upon a security violation. Protect drops packets, restrict drops and logs, shutdown disables the port.

stem: What is the difference between SPAN and RSPAN?
explanation: SPAN mirrors traffic to a local port on the same switch. RSPAN mirrors traffic across switches to a remote destination port using a dedicated RSPAN VLAN.

choices.text: SPAN is local; RSPAN mirrors across switches via a VLAN
SPAN is remote; RSPAN is local

stem: Which feature prevents a switch from becoming the root bridge by manipulating BPDUs?
explanation: Root Guard prevents a port from becoming a root port by putting it in root-inconsistent state if superior BPDUs are received, protecting the root bridge position.

stem: What does DHCP snooping do on a switch?
explanation: DHCP snooping acts as a firewall between untrusted hosts and DHCP servers, building a binding table of IP/MAC/port mappings to prevent rogue DHCP servers.

choices.text: Filters untrusted DHCP messages and builds a binding table

stem: What is the native VLAN used for on an 802.1Q trunk?
explanation: The native VLAN carries untagged traffic on an 802.1Q trunk. Frames in the native VLAN are not tagged.

stem: Which command enables PortFast on an interface?
explanation: PortFast allows an access port to transition immediately to forwarding state, skipping STP listening/learning phases. Configured with 'spanning-tree portfast'.

stem: What happens when BPDU Guard receives a BPDU on a PortFast-enabled port?
explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables the port if a BPDU is received, protecting against accidental switch connections to access ports.

choices.text: The port becomes a root port

stem: Which port security feature dynamically learns MAC addresses and saves them to the running config?
explanation: Sticky MAC addresses are learned dynamically and added to the running configuration, persisting across reboots if saved.

stem: What is the default administrative distance of a directly connected route?
explanation: A directly connected route has an administrative distance of 0, the most trustworthy source.

stem: Which OSPF area type does not allow external (Type 5) LSAs?
explanation: Stub areas block Type 5 (external) LSAs and use a default route instead. Totally stubby areas also block Type 3 summary LSAs.

stem: What is the OSPF DR/BDR election priority default value?
explanation: The default OSPF interface priority is 1. A priority of 0 makes a router ineligible to become DR/BDR.

stem: Which routing protocol uses DUAL (Diffusing Update Algorithm) to guarantee loop-free paths?
explanation: EIGRP uses DUAL to compute loop-free paths and provide fast convergence. It is an advanced distance-vector protocol.

stem: In EIGRP, what is the Feasible Distance (FD)?
explanation: Feasible Distance is the best (lowest) metric to reach a destination. The Reported Distance is the neighbor's metric to that destination.

choices.text: Best metric to reach the destination

stem: Which IPv6 routing protocol is the link-state protocol commonly used?
explanation: OSPFv3 is the IPv6 version of OSPF, a link-state routing protocol. EIGRP for IPv6 also exists but OSPFv3 is the standard link-state choice.

stem: What is the purpose of a floating static route?
explanation: A floating static route has a higher administrative distance than the primary route, so it only installs when the primary route is unavailable, providing backup.

choices.text: Backup route used when primary fails

stem: Which OSPF LSA type is flooded by an ASBR to advertise external routes?
explanation: Type 5 (AS External) LSAs are originated by an ASBR to advertise routes redistributed into OSPF from other routing domains.

stem: What is route summarization's primary benefit?
explanation: Route summarization reduces routing table size and LSA flooding, improving convergence and scalability.

choices.text: Eliminates the need for a default route

stem: Which protocol is used for first-hop redundancy and uses a virtual IP?
explanation: HSRP (Hot Standby Router Protocol) provides first-hop redundancy using a virtual IP and virtual MAC, with active/standby routers.

stem: In OSPF, what does the 'O IA' code in the routing table indicate?
explanation: O IA means OSPF Inter-Area route, learned from a summary LSA (Type 3) from another area.

stem: Which OSPF network type does not elect a DR/BDR?
explanation: Point-to-point and point-to-multipoint network types do not elect a DR/BDR, reducing overhead on those links.

stem: Which secure protocol is used to transfer files and is based on SSH?
explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) provides secure file transfer over an SSH connection. SCP is also SSH-based but SFTP is more feature-rich.

stem: Which ACL type can filter traffic based on source and destination IP and ports?
explanation: Extended ACLs (numbered 100-199, 2000-2699) can filter based on source/destination IP, protocol, and port numbers.

stem: What is the difference between a standard and extended ACL in terms of placement?
explanation: Standard ACLs should be placed close to the destination (they only filter source IP), while extended ACLs should be placed close to the source to save bandwidth.

choices.text: Standard near destination; Extended near source
Standard near source; Extended near destination

stem: Which VPN technology is commonly used for site-to-site connections and uses IPsec?
explanation: IPsec VPNs provide encrypted site-to-site tunnels. GRE over IPsec is common for carrying multicast/routing traffic.

stem: Which protocol provides centralized authentication for network devices using TCP port 49?
explanation: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49 and provides separate authentication, authorization, and accounting, commonly for device administration.

stem: What is the purpose of 802.1X in network security?
explanation: 802.1X provides port-based network access control, requiring authentication before granting network access.

stem: Which security feature validates DHCP messages and prevents rogue DHCP servers?
explanation: DHCP snooping validates DHCP messages and prevents rogue servers by trusting only designated ports.

stem: What does Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) protect against?
explanation: DAI validates ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding table, preventing ARP spoofing/poisoning attacks.

stem: Which protocol uses UDP port 161 for device management?
explanation: SNMP uses UDP 161 for queries and UDP 162 for traps. It is used for network device monitoring and management.

stem: Which DNS record type is used for email server routing?
explanation: MX (Mail Exchange) records specify the mail servers responsible for accepting email on behalf of a domain.

stem: Which RESTCONF operation uses HTTP GET to retrieve data?
explanation: RESTCONF maps CRUD operations to HTTP methods: GET retrieves, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH modifies, DELETE removes.

stem: Which protocol uses XML or JSON encoding and is used for network device configuration via RPC?
explanation: NETCONF uses RPC-based operations with XML or JSON encoding to configure and manage network devices, typically over SSH.

stem: What is streaming telemetry used for?
explanation: Streaming telemetry pushes real-time operational data from devices to collectors, enabling continuous monitoring without polling.

choices.text: Real-time push of device data to collectors

stem: Which IaC tool uses declarative configuration files to manage infrastructure?
explanation: Terraform uses HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) declarative files to define and provision infrastructure across providers.

stem: What is the purpose of AI output validation in network operations?
explanation: AI output validation ensures AI-generated configurations or recommendations are checked for correctness, safety, and compliance before deployment.

stem: Which YANG-based protocol provides a programmatic interface for network configuration?
explanation: NETCONF and RESTCONF both use YANG data models to define network configuration and operational data structures.

stem: Which tool is commonly used for network automation and configuration management using playbooks?
explanation: Ansible uses YAML playbooks to automate configuration management and network device provisioning.

stem: What is a benefit of using NETCONF over traditional CLI for device configuration?
explanation: NETCONF provides structured, transactional configuration with rollback capability and consistent data models, unlike CLI's text-based approach.

stem: Which data format is commonly used by RESTCONF for encoding?
explanation: RESTCONF supports JSON and XML encoding for representing YANG data. JSON is commonly used for REST APIs.

stem: What is the purpose of a YANG model in network management?
explanation: YANG is a data modeling language that defines the structure and constraints of configuration and operational data for network devices.

choices.text: Define data models for config and state

stem: Which streaming telemetry protocol uses gRPC and is vendor-neutral?
explanation: gNMI (gRPC Network Management Interface) uses gRPC for streaming telemetry and configuration, promoted by OpenConfig.

stem: What is a key consideration when validating AI-generated network configurations?
explanation: AI outputs must be validated against intended policy, syntax, and safety constraints before applying to production devices.

choices.text: Check against policy and syntax before apply
Skip review if confidence is high

stem: Which IPv6 header field replaces the IPv4 TTL field?
explanation: IPv6 uses the Hop Limit field instead of TTL. It is decremented by each router and the packet is discarded when it reaches zero.

stem: What is the purpose of the IPv6 Flow Label field?
explanation: The Flow Label identifies a sequence of packets requiring special handling (e.g., QoS) by routers, enabling efficient forwarding without deep inspection.

choices.text: Identify packets needing special router handling

stem: Which wireless standard introduced Target Wake Time (TWT) to improve battery life for IoT devices?
explanation: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) introduced TWT, allowing devices to negotiate wake/sleep schedules to conserve power.

stem: In a three-tier campus design, which layer aggregates traffic from the access layer and applies policies?
explanation: The distribution layer aggregates access-layer traffic, applies routing policies, and provides redundancy between access and core.

stem: Which IPv6 address type is used for one-to-nearest communication to the closest interface?
explanation: Anycast addresses are assigned to multiple interfaces; packets are delivered to the nearest one based on routing metrics.

stem: What is the primary benefit of cloud-managed networking for branch offices?
explanation: Cloud management provides centralized visibility, zero-touch provisioning, and simplified operations without on-site controllers.
